bindings.label: Patient presented with tension-like headaches for several months, unrelieved by medical treatment
Patient is a male veteran in his 40s with a history of posttraumatic stress disorder, traumatic brain injury, and chronic headaches
Patient had undergone tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in childhood and reported no sinonasal symptoms, radiation exposure, or trauma
Head and neck examination including flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed bilateral fullness of the nasopharynx, with submucosal lesions appearing to be within the torus tubarii
MRI shows bilateral submucosal lesions in the torus tubarii with restricted diffusion
Biopsy of the nasopharyngeal lesion reveals benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and mild chronic inflammation
Endoscopy shows an enlarged cystic torus tubarius with purulent drainage
The nasopharyngeal lesions are benign reactive inflammatory lesions
Chronic tension-like headaches are caused by benign inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesions
